full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J.: This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal has arisen out of the order dated 27.01.2022 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.52179 of 2021 arising out of Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.03 of 2021 arose from Nagarkanda Police Station Case No.09 dated 11.08.2019 corresponding to G.R. No.190 of 2019 under sections 143/341/323/326/307/302/ 506/114/34 of the Penal Code, now pending before the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka. 

 2. The accused-respondents filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.52179 of 2021 in Tender No.60046 of 2021 before the High Court Division under section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for transfer-ring the Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.03 of 2021 arising out of Nagarkanda Police Station Case No.09 dated 11.08.2019 corresponding to G.R. No.190 of 2019 under sections 143/341/323/ 326/307/302/506/ 114/34 of the Penal Code from the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka to any other Tribunal having competent jurisdiction. 

 3. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 11.08.2019, one Md. Raihan Uddin Mia as informant lodged the instant First Information Report (FIR) with the Nagarkanda Police Station implicating all 21 persons as accused and some 8 to 10 anonymous persons alleging inter alia that, due to resistance against the illegal works of Hanif Mia alias Hridoy, there was an enmity between the informant and the said Hanif Mia, which reached to the extreme later on. As a result of that enmity, on 10.08.2019 when the informant and others got out from the mosque after saying their prayers and went to the east side of the mosque, the accused persons being armed with various fire and local arms attacked the victims namely Rowshan Ali, Mirajul Islam Tuhin and others. The moment victims raised a hue and cry seeking help, the local people came forward, as a result the accused persons fled away. Subsequently, the victims were taken to Faridpur General Hospital, wherein the doctors on duty declared the victims Rowshan Ali Mia and Mirajul Islam Tuhin dead. The other victims namely Golam Rasul and Golam Mowla were sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for better treatment. Being recovered after getting treatment the informant lodged the FIR, which was registered as Nagarkanda Police Station Case No.09 dated 11.08.2019 corresponding to G.R. No.190 of 2019 under sections 143/341/323/ 326/ 307/ 302/ 506/ 114/ 34 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Later on after a thorough investigation the police submitted charge sheet being No.98 dated 22.07.2020 under sections 143/341/323/326/307/302/506/114/34 of the Penal Code against the accused per-sons. Subsequently the said charge sheet was accepted by the Court. 

 5. Thereafter, the case was duly sent to the Druto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka (hereinafter called as Tribunal) for trial in accordance with law. The case was renumbered as Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.03 of 2021. During trial before the Tribunal on 19.10.2021 the accused per-sons filed three separate applications i.e. application for adjournment, application for bail and application for discharge of the accused persons under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. But the Tribunal on same day after hearing both the parties rejected all three applications and took cognizance and framed charge against the accused persons under sections 143/341/323/326/307/302/506/114/34 of the Penal Code. 

 8. Mr. A.M. Amin Uddin, the learned Attorney General appearing for the petitioner took us through the order of the High Court Division dated 27.01.2022 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.52179 of 2021, the materials on record and submits that the High Court Division has not applied its judicial mind having failed to appreciate that accused-respondents are named in the FIR having strong prima facie allegation and specific overt act of committing heinous offences under sections 143/341/323/326/307/302/506/114/34 of the Penal Code. He further submits that the High Court Division committed gross error in not following the settled principle of the decision of the apex Court that an application under 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before taking cognizance of a case is not maintainable.
